video.title: The Most Profitable Side Hustle to Start With No Money

summary: Brothers Jackson and Carson describe wholesaling vacant land by finding home builders first, learning their buying criteria, then contracting with landowners and assigning the contracts to those builders. They say the business can start with a phone and internet, while their scaled operation used direct mail, callers, software, and a small team. They explain how they price deals, screen land, manage contracts, and use referrals, and they compare land wholesaling with house wholesaling and property flipping. The key takeaway is to find a real buyer before making offers, price accurately, and build the skill by doing the work consistently.

ideas.name: Builder-first vacant land wholesaling
ideas.one_liner: Find a builder's land buy box, contract suitable vacant land below that price, and assign the contract to the builder for a spread.
ideas.business_model: Assignment fee or margin between the seller's contract price and the builder's purchase price.
ideas.customer: Home builders buying scattered lots, plus landowners willing to sell vacant land.
ideas.problem: Builders need lots that fit their locations and specifications; some landowners want a quicker sale without agent fees and a long listing period.
ideas.offer: Source a suitable lot, agree a price with the owner, and assign the purchase contract to a builder already interested in that type of lot.

pricing.model: Keep the difference between the contracted seller price and the builder's price; the speakers also describe some deals as a percentage of the builder's price.

price_points.label: Average deal profit claimed by the guests
Typical transparent margin described by the guests
Typical offer range described by the guests

pricing.notes: Prices depend on location, lot characteristics, buyer criteria, and negotiation. The speakers describe 90–95% margins for their operation, but do not define the margin calculation.

acquisition_channels.details: Contact builders first, including builders identified from newly built homes listed for sale on Zillow, and ask for their buy box: location, lot size, and price.

quote.text: you go on Zillow and you filter it by houses built in 2025 or 2026, right? For sale.
quote.speaker: Jackson

acquisition_channels.details: Mail owners an introduction letter and a contract with an offer, company information, and a request to call or email. The guests say some signed contracts came back without a prior conversation.

quote.text: My favorite is actually direct mail. So, we'll send them a one-page introduction letter and then we'll send them a contract.
quote.speaker: Jackson

acquisition_channels.details: Call landowners to ask whether they would sell, explain the net cash offer and closing terms, and make a specific offer. The guests also used overseas callers at scale.

quote.text: Hey, Chris. Is this the owner of 123 Main Street? Awesome. I I was reaching out. Would any chance would you be open to selling this property
quote.speaker: Carson

acquisition_channels.details: The guests previously sent large volumes of text offers in selected US states, but say they stopped texting to limit liability and warn that rules vary. This channel cannot be copied into the UK without consent and legal review.

quote.text: So, to send 50,000 messages a month, it's about 1,200 bucks a month to send.
quote.speaker: Jackson

acquisition_channels.details: Monitor newly listed land in a target market and make an early offer before other buyers respond; the guests describe using listing alerts.

quote.text: if I just go and I have notifications on and first thing in the morning and as the new ones come in
quote.speaker: Jackson

acquisition_channels.details: After closing, send a handwritten thank-you letter and offer a referral payment if a referred owner completes a deal.

quote.text: if you refer a family member or a friend to sell their property with us and we get a deal done, we'll send you $1,000 in cash
quote.speaker: Jackson

ideas.delivery: The operators identify and qualify land virtually, agree an assignable purchase contract with the landowner, then assign it to a builder and send the contracts and deal details to a title company. They say their team checks title progress and keeps buyers and sellers updated; the builder decides whether to proceed after reviewing or driving by the lot.
unit_economics_claims: The guests claim an average gross profit of about $8,600 per deal.
They claim their operation has 90–95% margins, without defining the calculation.
They say one deal can take them 30 minutes to an hour of their own time.
They describe examples where a 10% spread on a $750,000 lot would yield $75,000.
ideas.startup_cost: The guests say it can be started with an iPhone and internet connection and describe a free-start workflow. No typical startup cost is stated.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: No typical timeline is stated. The guests describe one free-start participant earning an assignment fee within 14 days.

acquisition.how: Software can build lists, enrich owner records, prepare mail, and monitor listings. Finding a suitable builder, checking records, and negotiating with owners still need human judgement. In the UK, unsolicited marketing texts, WhatsApp messages, DMs, and emails to individuals and sole traders require consent; cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS.

onboarding.how: Forms, e-signatures, reminders, and data entry can be automated, but contract terms, authority to assign, title issues, and local legal requirements need human review.

delivery.how: Agents can assemble parcel data, compare buyer criteria, and coordinate documents. A person still needs to check suitability, resolve exceptions, and handle buyer and seller decisions; physical inspections may be needed.

billing.how: A title or escrow provider handles closing and disburses the assignment proceeds. Software can track milestones and reconcile the payment, with a human checking the closing statement.

support.how: Routine status updates and reminders can be automated, but negotiations, title problems, and trust-sensitive conversations need a person.

uk_applicability.notes: The buyer-first land sourcing model could be adapted to UK land and developers, but the speakers' US contracts, title-company workflow, datasets, and market examples do not transfer directly. UK property, planning, title, data-protection, and marketing rules need local review.

risks: A buyer may reject a lot after reviewing slope, wetlands, protected wildlife, utilities, access, or other site constraints.
The guests say overpricing a contract can make it difficult to assign; they warn against mass-sending offers above plausible value.
Land conditions and local rules vary by state and market; they recommend learning the local checks and doing due diligence before making offers.
The guests say their model is difficult to sell as an exit and that high profits created a large tax bill for them.
The guests say they no longer use mass texting because they wanted to limit their liability. UK unsolicited marketing texts to individuals and sole traders require consent.
The business depends on reliable buyers and on the seller understanding the assignment arrangement; the guests advocate being transparent about their role and margin.

ideas.name: Buy land outright and resell it
ideas.one_liner: Purchase a parcel or package of lots, then resell it for more after checking its value and buyer demand.
ideas.business_model: Buy land with the operator's own funds, then resell it for a profit.
ideas.customer: Home builders or other land buyers; the original seller is the source of the land.
ideas.problem: A seller may want to sell a package of lots, while the operator sees resale value that has not yet been established.
ideas.offer: Buy the land directly and sell it to a buyer after confirming its likely value and suitability.

pricing.model: One-off purchase and resale with the operator retaining the resale proceeds after purchase and transaction costs.
pricing.notes: The guests say the lots sold for a little over $180,000 and later describe the sale as about $185,000–$190,000 before closing costs and agent payment.

acquisition_channels.details: The seller contacted the guests after receiving their postcards inviting owners to get in touch.

quote.text: So, we would send like postcards. Hey, reach out if you're interested. Um, and she called me
quote.speaker: Jackson

ideas.delivery: The guests used their own funds to close on four lots, then sold them to buyers after calling real estate agents to estimate the lots' values. They describe paying closing costs and an agent on the resale.
unit_economics_claims: The guests say they bought four lots for $37,000 and made about $140,000 on the deal.
They say the lots sold for a little over $180,000, with closing costs and an agent paid from the proceeds.
tools: stock market investments used as the source of funds
ideas.startup_cost: Requires purchase capital; the guests say they liquidated their stock investments to fund this deal.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: They say the deal came about six months into the business; the time from purchase to resale is not stated.

acquisition.how: Mailing and owner research can be supported by software, but sourcing and evaluating a specific parcel still require human judgement.

onboarding.how: A human must negotiate the purchase, fund it, and review the purchase documents.

delivery.how: A person must assess the parcel, manage the resale, and coordinate closing; land issues can require local checks.

billing.how: A title company can process closing and payment, but the operator must fund the acquisition and check the settlement.

support.how: Seller, agent, and buyer questions and negotiations are handled by people.

uk_applicability.notes: Buying and reselling land is possible in the UK, but the deal economics, conveyancing, planning status, taxes, and buyer market differ from the Florida example.

risks: The operators had to tie up their own capital and say they liquidated stocks to complete the purchase.
The guests initially did not know how to value the lots and sought multiple agents' opinions.
Closing costs and agent fees reduced the gross resale proceeds.

ideas.name: House wholesaling
ideas.one_liner: Contract to buy a house at one price and assign the contract to an investor for a higher price without taking ownership.
ideas.business_model: Assignment fee between the seller's contract price and the investor's price.
ideas.problem: A seller wants to sell a house, while an investor wants an acquisition at a price that leaves room for a renovation and resale.
ideas.offer: Find a seller, sign an assignable contract, then find an investor willing to pay more for the right to buy the property.

pricing.notes: The host describes earnest money and a 30-, 60-, 90-, or 120-day period to find a buyer as part of a typical example.

acquisition_channels.details: The host mentions postcards and yellow letters as ways house wholesalers find off-market properties.

quote.text: Postcards, yellow letters, cold calling, whatever. Looking at the MLS, and you will try to get them under contract.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Cold calls are mentioned as an off-market seller acquisition method.

quote.text: Postcards, yellow letters, cold calling, whatever. Looking at the MLS, and you will try to get them under contract.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: The wholesaler arranges an assignable contract, finds an investor, and sends the contracts to a title company for closing. The seller receives the agreed price and the wholesaler receives the difference.
unit_economics_claims: The host gives an illustrative $10,000 spread between a $200,000 seller price and a $210,000 buyer price.
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated; the host says a wholesaler may put up earnest money.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated; the host gives example contract periods of 30, 60, 90, or 120 days.

acquisition.how: List building and mail preparation can be automated, but seller conversations and deal qualification remain human. UK calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS; marketing messages to individuals and sole traders need consent.

onboarding.how: Document generation and signatures can be automated, but contract terms and assignment rights need legal review.

delivery.how: House condition, inspections, occupants, and buyer coordination require substantial human work.

billing.how: A title company can process payment, with human oversight of the closing.

support.how: Seller and investor conversations, inspections, and exceptions require a person.

uk_applicability.notes: The broad contract-assignment concept may be adaptable, but US wholesaling forms, title workflows, and real estate practices differ. UK legal and consumer rules need specialist review.

risks: The host says the wholesaler can lose earnest money if they fail to find a buyer within the contract period.
The guests say house deals can involve inspections, repairs, occupant moves, and buyers attempting to renegotiate.
Cold outreach must comply with applicable UK marketing rules.

tactics.name: Start with the builder's buy box
steps: Identify builders that sell newly built homes, using listings as a lead source.
Ask what locations, lot sizes, and prices the builder will accept.
Record the criteria and buying contact in a simple spreadsheet.
Only source parcels that match the stated requirements.

quote.text: So the first thing, the way we do it with the builder first method is you get the builder's buy box.
quote.speaker: Jackson

tactics.name: Find owners and make offers below the buyer price
steps: Build a list of owners whose parcels match the builder's buy box.
Prioritise owners who have held the property for a long time and paid less, as the guests describe.
Use parcel records and owner lookup tools to find contact details.
Calculate an offer that leaves a spread while still making sense against current alternatives.

quote.text: And then we would reverse engineer it, go find sellers, go pull a list of owners that are offmarket properties
quote.speaker: Jackson

tactics.name: Use consistent lot criteria for batch offers
steps: Choose a market with multiple builders and repeated, similar parcels.
Group parcels by location and lot characteristics.
Avoid mixing parcels with materially different sizes or conditions in one offer campaign.
The guests say similar parcels let them make many consistent offers.

quote.text: So I want to send a thousand offers at once. I can't do that if every lot's different.
quote.speaker: Jackson

tactics.name: Use direct mail with an offer and contract
steps: Send a one-page introduction to the owner.
Include the offer and purchase contract in the mailing.
Give the owner a phone number and email to respond.
Track signed contracts and follow up on responses.

quote.text: we'll send them a one-page introduction letter and then we'll send them a contract. And on that contract, I'll put our offer on it.
quote.speaker: Jackson

tactics.name: Explain the seller's net proceeds
steps: Compare the offer with the seller's likely net after agent fees and closing costs.
Explain the time difference between a direct close and a listing, using specific local comparisons only when known.
State the amount offered, the expected closing time, and who pays closing costs.
Do not claim a buyer is ready unless one has actually been lined up.

quote.text: And when you explain it like that, like they actually are benefiting from it. You already have somebody lined up and you're not really messing with them
quote.speaker: Jackson

tactics.name: Keep seller outreach honest
steps: Tell the seller that you work with builders and intend to assign or pass the property to a builder.
Explain the intended margin where relevant, as the guests say they do.
Do not pretend to be the builder or misrepresent who will buy the property.
Make offers that can be completed and disclose material uncertainty.

quote.text: We have always taken an honest approach. anybody we've taught to do this, we tell them to be honest
quote.speaker: Jackson

tactics.name: Use a contract feasibility period and buyer deposit
steps: The guests say their seller contract includes a feasibility study through the closing date.
They say earnest money is not due until closing under their contract.
They make sure the builder's assignment contract has a due date for its earnest money.
Confirm contract terms with qualified local counsel before using them.

quote.text: And we have a feasibility study. That means we can back out to the day of the closing date with no risk.
quote.speaker: Jackson

tactics.name: Check land constraints before closing
steps: Check aerial imagery and local records for wetlands, slope, utilities, access, wildlife, and other constraints mentioned by builders.
Ask the city or county what reports are available when a local term is unfamiliar.
Confirm parcel-specific concerns with the builder before relying on a contract.
Use a termination right if the parcel fails the stated feasibility checks.

quote.text: you just basically just call the city and say, "What does this mean? How do I get a report for it?"
quote.speaker: Jackson

tactics.name: Call neighbouring owners before a sale
steps: Look up the owners of neighbouring parcels after securing a deal.
Contact them as a courtesy and explain that a builder may buy the land.
Ask whether they would like to extend their yard or buy the lot.
Do not assume a neighbour will pay more; check whether they have interest and funds.

quote.text: the first thing I do is I call the neighboring houses, right? Because the most annoying thing is a homeowner.
quote.speaker: Jackson

tactics.name: Ask for a meaningful referral
steps: After closing, send a handwritten thank-you letter.
Ask the seller to refer a friend or family member who may sell land.
Offer a stated cash payment only if the referral results in a completed deal.
Track referral source and closing so the reward is paid consistently.

tactics.name: Keep leads warm after an initial no
steps: If the owner rejects the offer, stay polite and invite them to save the caller's details.
Explain that the price may change and that the business continues to buy land.
Record the conversation and follow up only through a lawful channel.
Revisit the lead if the owner gets in touch later.

evidence_quality.rationale: The guests present themselves as first-hand operators and give detailed workflows, deal examples, and operating figures. The claims are self-reported, some figures are approximate or lack definitions, and the transcript contains obvious transcription errors. The host and guests also promote paid or owned products and communities.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: The guests promote Buyer Bridge, their own software, and Carson and Jackson communities. The host includes sponsor and promotional reads for Beehiiv, paid business plans, and Playmakers AI; these were not treated as business ideas.
